items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: I later joined her as her pianist and arranger and we toured all over the RKO theatres

ctx.x: Charlie told her what was happening. They went downstairs, and rehearsed, and she said, 'Well I don't have any gowns, or anything.' She said, 'I just came to New York to visit,' so he gave her some money to go out and get a gown, and she went in the next show. And broke it up of course, and we rehearsed a couple of things downstairs, like 'The Captain and His Men,' and some other great things. She ad libbed a few things. So to make a long story short, we were set for the Paramount Theatre. So we went to the…

Charlie always liked to play the horses. He had a wire on the back stage to the race track, and he won, and came across the stage and threw hundred dollar bills at the guys, and all this kind of stuff. He was quite a guy. He was funny, you know, and anyway, Lena went on and broke it up there, and of course, the scouts saw her and she went to Hollywood to the Trocadero out there. I don't need to say anything else about it, except I later joined her as her pianist and arranger and we toured all over the RKO…
there to Fort Dix, and all these places, all in a day. You know, we played sometimes -- it was a great experience for me. So this is what Charley Barnet did for me.
